# Ricardo Custódio

I am a professor and researcher in computer science, working primarily
in information security and cryptography. My research spans digital
signatures, public key infrastructure, digital identity, electronic
documents, cryptographic protocols, post-quantum cryptography,
finite-field arithmetic, and artificial intelligence applied to security.

I am a Full Professor at the Department of Informatics and Statistics
of the Federal University of Santa Catarina (UFSC), in Florianópolis,
Brazil, and supervisor of the Computer Security Laboratory (LabSEC).

Throughout my academic career, I have combined fundamental and applied
research with the development of technologies and infrastructures for
real-world digital trust systems.

## Academic trajectory

I received my Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering from the
Federal University of Santa Catarina (UFSC), followed by a Master's
degree in Electrical Engineering at the same university.

I received my PhD in Computer Science from the Federal University of
Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) in 1999.

I joined UFSC as a faculty member in 1994. Over the following decades,
my academic activities have included teaching, research, technology
development, graduate supervision, and collaboration with public and
private institutions.

## Research

My work is centered on the security and trust mechanisms required for
digital systems.

My main research interests include:

- information security;
- cryptography and cryptographic protocols;
- digital signatures and electronic signatures;
- public key infrastructure (PKI);
- digital identity and authentication;
- electronic documents and long-term preservation;
- cryptographic key management;
- arithmetic over finite fields;
- post-quantum cryptography;
- artificial intelligence applied to security and digital trust.

A recurring theme in my research is the connection between
**cryptographic foundations and deployable systems**: how mathematical,
cryptographic and security mechanisms can be transformed into
infrastructures and applications that operate in real institutional
environments.

## LabSEC

I supervise the **Computer Security Laboratory (LabSEC)** at UFSC.

LabSEC conducts research and technology development in information
security and cryptography, bringing together undergraduate, Master's
and PhD students and collaborating with universities, government
institutions and organizations involved in digital infrastructures.

Over the years, the laboratory has worked on topics including public
key infrastructure, digital certification, digital signatures,
electronic documents, digital identity, cryptographic protocols,
blockchain technologies and post-quantum cryptography.

## Students and supervision

An important part of my academic work has been the education and
supervision of researchers.

I supervise undergraduate research, Master's dissertations and PhD
theses, particularly in information security, cryptography, digital
identity and trustworthy digital infrastructures.

Many of the research projects developed with students combine
theoretical investigation with the design, implementation and
experimental evaluation of security technologies.

[Students and supervision →](supervision.qmd)

## Beyond the university

My work also involves research, development and innovation projects
with institutions outside the university.

These collaborations have provided opportunities to apply research in
areas such as digital certification, electronic documents, civil
registration, digital identity, financial infrastructures and
post-quantum security.
